pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 1.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you ensure that you benefit from a reading session?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify a variety of texts for independent reading
2. read selected materials for information and enjoyment
3. appreciate the value of independent reading in lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 1.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 1.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify a variety of texts for independent reading

What this means
In this part you learn to identify a variety of texts for independent reading. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify a variety of texts for independent reading.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify a variety of texts for independent reading. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read selected materials for information and enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to read selected materials for information and enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read selected materials for information and enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read selected materials for information and enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the value of independent reading in lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the value of independent reading in lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the value of independent reading in lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the value of independent reading in lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify a variety of texts for independent reading)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a partner. (skill: read selected materials for information and enjoyment)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the value of independent reading in lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify a variety of texts for independent reading.
3. Practise this skill: read selected materials for information and enjoyment.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the value of independent reading in lifelong learning.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you ensure that you benefit from a reading session?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify a variety of texts for independent reading.
5. Be able to: read selected materials for information and enjoyment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
